title: Everyday Worship
description: General User → Mid. Familiar worship knowledge, broader basics and short everyday applications. Covers purification, congregational prayer, regular additional prayers, Ramadan, charity, supplication and remembrance. All questions are Mid level; detailed school-specific rulings and individual fatwas are outside the scope.
levelMethod: Mid describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires more understanding and simple connections than Beginner, without specialist study. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: In Uthman's demonstration of the Prophet's wudu, what did he wash before rinsing his mouth and nose?

options.text: His hands
His feet
His face
His forearms

questions.explanation: Uthman began by washing his hands, then rinsed his mouth and nose as part of the demonstrated wudu.

questions.question: Which washing pattern is also reported in the Prophet's wudu?

options.text: Washing every part at least five times
Washing each part that is washed once
Washing only the face once
Skipping the feet whenever water is cold

questions.explanation: A report describes the Prophet performing wudu with one washing of each part that is washed. One complete washing is different from leaving an area dry.

questions.question: Which prayer does the cited hadith especially praise after the obligatory prayers?

options.text: Only prayer offered on journeys
Only prayer offered outdoors
Prayer during the night
Prayer performed as quickly as possible

questions.explanation: The hadith gives special merit to night prayer after the prescribed prayers.

questions.question: Which action appears in the reported demonstration of wudu?

options.text: Washing the hair with soap
Changing into new clothes
Applying perfume to the hands
Rinsing the mouth and nose

questions.explanation: Rinsing the mouth and nose appears in Uthman's account of the Prophet's wudu.

questions.question: How many additional daily rakahs are especially encouraged in Umm Habibah's report?

options.text: Twelve
Five
Seven
Twenty

questions.explanation: The report encourages twelve daily rakahs beyond the obligatory prayers. These are additional worship, not a replacement for the obligatory prayers.

questions.question: How many rakahs are in the Sunnah prayer associated with Fajr?

options.text: Three
Two
Four
Six

questions.explanation: The hadith highlights the great virtue of the two Sunnah rakahs of Fajr.

questions.question: What prayer does the cited hadith encourage on entering a mosque before sitting?

options.text: A second complete Friday prayer
A compulsory four-rakah prayer for every visit
Two rakahs
A prayer performed only once in a lifetime

questions.explanation: The report encourages two rakahs before sitting upon entering a mosque. Detailed questions about timing and circumstances need appropriate guidance.

questions.question: In congregational prayer, whom should worshippers follow in the prayer movements?

options.text: The person who moves fastest
The nearest person regardless of the imam
Whoever arrived first
The imam leading them

questions.explanation: The imam is appointed to lead, and the congregation is instructed to follow his movements.

questions.question: What is the sermon delivered as part of Jumuah commonly called?

options.text: The khutbah
The iqamah
The suhur
The tashahhud

questions.explanation: The khutbah is the Friday sermon. The cited report stresses attentive listening while it is being delivered.

questions.question: Tarawih is associated with additional night prayer during which month?

options.text: Muharram only
Ramadan
Shawwal only
Dhul-Hijjah only

questions.explanation: Tarawih is the familiar name for Ramadan night prayer. The hadith encourages standing in prayer during Ramadan with faith and hope of reward.

questions.question: Which practice involves a devotional retreat in the mosque, especially associated with Ramadan's last ten days?

options.text: Zakat al-fitr
The adhan
I'tikaf
The khutbah

questions.explanation: Aishah reports that the Prophet observed i'tikaf during Ramadan's last ten days.

questions.question: When did the Prophet especially direct Muslims to seek Laylat al-Qadr?

options.text: Only the first night of Ramadan
The first Friday of every month
The daytime of Eid al-Fitr
The odd nights of Ramadan's last ten nights

questions.explanation: The report directs believers to seek Laylat al-Qadr in the odd nights of Ramadan's final ten nights.

questions.question: On which two days did the Prophet prohibit fasting?

options.text: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
The first and last Mondays of each month
Every Friday and Saturday
The first and last days of Ramadan

questions.explanation: The two Eid days themselves are days on which fasting is prohibited. This is different from the rules for surrounding days.

questions.question: Which month is singled out for the merit of fasting after Ramadan?

options.text: Shawwal alone
Muharram
Rajab alone
Rabi al-Awwal

questions.explanation: The hadith gives special merit to fasting in Muharram after Ramadan. This does not make a whole month of fasting obligatory.

questions.question: When did the Prophet instruct that zakat al-fitr be given in relation to the Eid prayer?

options.text: Only after the Eid prayer finishes
Only after the month following Ramadan ends
Before people go out to the Eid prayer
Only during the Hajj sermon

questions.explanation: The cited report directs that zakat al-fitr be given before people go out to the Eid prayer.

questions.question: In discussions of zakah, what does nisab refer to?

options.text: A special prayer before giving money
The name of a charity recipient
A fixed fee charged by every mosque
A minimum qualifying amount of relevant wealth

questions.explanation: The hadith describes minimum amounts below which certain kinds of wealth are not subject to zakah. Nisab refers to a qualifying threshold.

questions.question: Which practice is encouraged after obligatory prayers in the cited hadith?

options.text: Remembering Allah with words of praise
Repeating the obligatory prayer immediately
Treating all further supplication as forbidden
Delaying the next prayer until midnight

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches remembrance after prayer, including glorifying, praising and magnifying Allah.

questions.question: Which attitude does the Prophet warn against when making dua?

options.text: Asking Allah with hope
Giving up impatiently because an answer seems delayed
Continuing to ask Allah
Recognizing one's need for Allah

questions.explanation: The warning concerns impatience that leads a person to say they asked but received no answer.

questions.question: What does La ilaha illa Allah affirm?

options.text: Every wish is guaranteed immediately
A person no longer needs to pray
None is worthy of worship except Allah
Only one language can be used for every dua

questions.explanation: This phrase affirms Allah's exclusive right to worship. It is among the beloved words of remembrance mentioned in the hadith.

questions.question: What do Muslims ask Allah to grant the Prophet when sending salawat?

options.text: Forgiveness for Allah
A share in Allah's divinity
Permission to replace revelation
Blessings

questions.explanation: The verse instructs believers to send blessings and greetings of peace upon the Prophet.

questions.question: Why is one complete washing different from a quick splash that leaves part of a limb dry?

options.text: Completeness matters, not just how many times water is applied
Saying a number aloud completes the washing
Any splash counts even if no water reaches the skin
Repeating a motion removes the need for water

questions.explanation: The report of washing once concerns an actual washing, not missing the area that must be washed.

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from the small amount of water used for the Prophet's wudu?

options.text: More water always means more reward
Clean thoroughly while using water carefully
Wudu requires a large bucket every time
Careful water use means leaving required areas dry

questions.explanation: The report shows that wudu can be completed with a modest amount of water. Thoroughness and careful use can go together.

questions.question: A person is certain of having wudu but only suspects it may have broken. What principle does the cited report teach?

options.text: Every passing thought requires fresh wudu
Wudu always expires after a few minutes
Mere suspicion does not cancel established certainty
The nearest person's opinion decides whether it broke

questions.explanation: The report protects a person from acting on mere doubt. Sound and smell are examples of clear evidence, not the only possible ways of knowing that wind passed.

questions.question: What does following the imam mean for bowing and prostration?

options.text: Trying to finish every movement before him
Choosing a separate sequence of movements
Following whichever worshipper is easiest to see, even against the imam
Letting the imam lead rather than deliberately moving ahead

questions.explanation: The report instructs worshippers to follow the imam in prayer rather than race ahead.

questions.question: How should someone approach a congregational prayer that has already begun?

options.text: Calmly, joining what they catch and completing what they missed
By running and pushing through the rows
By waiting outside until everyone finishes
By assuming missed prayer can never be completed

questions.explanation: The Prophet instructed worshippers to approach with calmness, join what they reach and complete what they miss.

questions.question: Why should ordinary conversation stop during the Friday khutbah?

options.text: The sermon is only background sound
Attentive listening is required, even a spoken correction can become idle talk
Talking makes the sermon shorter
Only conversations about money should stop

questions.explanation: The report warns that even telling a companion to be quiet during the khutbah is idle talk. It emphasizes listening rather than ordinary conversation.

questions.question: How do the additional daily prayers relate to the obligatory prayers?

options.text: They cancel the obligation of the five prayers
They become obligatory only when done publicly
They add worship alongside the obligatory prayers
They may replace any missed obligatory prayer automatically

questions.explanation: Umm Habibah's report expressly distinguishes these additional rakahs from the obligatory prayers.

questions.question: Which intention is emphasized for Ramadan night prayer in the cited report?

options.text: Winning praise for staying awake longest
Completing it only to impress friends
Treating it as a competition for attention
Faith and hope of reward from Allah

questions.explanation: The report links Ramadan night prayer with faith and seeking Allah's reward.

questions.question: Which description best fits the Prophet's reported i'tikaf practice?

options.text: Setting aside Ramadan's last ten days for a devotional retreat
Replacing Ramadan fasting with a holiday
Holding an annual business exhibition in the mosque
Ending all prayer during the final ten days

questions.explanation: The report describes a repeated devotional practice during Ramadan's final ten days.

questions.question: How does the Quran describe the merit of Laylat al-Qadr?

options.text: Exactly equal to any ordinary afternoon
Better than a thousand months
Less valuable than every other Ramadan night
Important only for people who know its exact date

questions.explanation: The Quran describes the night as better than a thousand months. Its value encourages worship rather than certainty about a single calendar date.

questions.question: What distinction does the hadith about the five daily prayers make?

options.text: Every additional prayer replaces an obligatory one
Only the prayers offered in a mosque are obligatory
The five daily prayers are obligatory; additional prayers are voluntary
There is no difference between obligatory and additional prayer

questions.explanation: The report identifies the five daily prayers as the required daily prayers and distinguishes additional voluntary worship.

questions.question: What does the teaching approved in the Salman and Abu al-Darda story show about worship?

options.text: More voluntary worship always justifies neglecting dependants
Sleep is incompatible with sincere worship
Family responsibilities must end during voluntary fasting
Worship should respect the rights of Allah, oneself and one's family

questions.explanation: The Prophet approved Salman's reminder that these rights should all be given their due.

questions.question: Why does a good intention not make fasting on Eid al-Fitr acceptable?

options.text: Worship follows its prescribed limits, including days when fasting is prohibited
Good intentions make all timing rules irrelevant
Eid fasting is required only for adults
The prohibition applies only to people attending Eid prayer

questions.explanation: The Prophet prohibited fasting on the two Eid days. An intention to do extra worship does not remove that prohibition.

questions.question: Why is it inaccurate to assume every person with any savings owes the same amount of zakah?

options.text: Zakah is always a flat admission fee
Zakah has qualifying conditions and thresholds
The number of banknotes alone determines the amount
Every small gift automatically settles all zakah

questions.explanation: The cited report sets thresholds for specified kinds of wealth. Actual assessment requires checking the relevant conditions for one's wealth.

questions.question: Which planning principle follows from the instruction about zakat al-fitr?

options.text: Wait until the prayer is over before thinking about it
Assume a promise to donate next year is sufficient
Arrange its delivery early enough to meet the time before Eid prayer
Treat the time of payment as unrelated to the practice

questions.explanation: Planning ahead helps fulfil the reported instruction to give zakat al-fitr before people go out to the Eid prayer.

questions.question: What does Quran 2:267 teach about choosing goods to give?

options.text: Always give away items one would refuse to accept oneself
The recipient's needs never matter
Only items with a famous brand can be given
Give from good things rather than deliberately selecting inferior items

questions.explanation: The verse warns against deliberately selecting poor-quality things that one would be reluctant to accept.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects Quran 2:271 about public and private charity?

options.text: Public charity can be good, and giving privately to the poor is better
All public charity is automatically hypocrisy
Private charity is never rewarded
Charity is accepted only if the donor's name is announced

questions.explanation: The verse acknowledges public charity as good while praising giving privately to the poor. Visibility alone does not prove someone's intention.

questions.question: What does patience in dua involve?

options.text: Setting a deadline after which Allah must grant the request
Continuing to turn to Allah without demanding an immediate answer
Concluding that delay proves Allah did not hear
Refusing to ask again after the first attempt

questions.explanation: The hadith warns against impatiently abandoning supplication because an answer seems delayed.

questions.question: Which understanding of remembrance is supported by Quran 3:191?

options.text: Remembrance is possible only while standing in a mosque
Sitting makes every form of remembrance invalid
Allah can be remembered while standing, sitting or lying down
Remembrance is limited to the moments immediately after prayer

questions.explanation: The verse describes people remembering Allah in different postures, showing that remembrance can accompany daily life.

questions.question: What does khushu in prayer especially concern?

options.text: Finishing before everyone else
Making every movement unusually loud
Ensuring other people notice one's devotion
Humble attentiveness before Allah

questions.explanation: The verses praise believers who have humility and attentiveness in their prayers.

questions.question: A friend says night prayer is valuable, so the five obligatory prayers can be skipped. What is the best response?

options.text: Night prayer has great merit, while the obligatory prayers remain required
One night prayer replaces the whole next day
Only night prayer counts during busy weeks
The five daily prayers apply only in Ramadan

questions.explanation: The merit of night prayer does not remove the obligation of the five daily prayers.

questions.question: A learner washes each part that needs washing once, fully, and completes wudu correctly. Someone says it must always be three times. Which response fits the report?

options.text: Three is the minimum for every washing in all circumstances
One complete washing is also reported from the Prophet
The learner must start again solely because each was washed once
One washing is allowed only on Fridays

questions.explanation: The report establishes wudu with one washing of each part that is washed. The question assumes the wudu was otherwise completed correctly.

questions.question: The tap is running strongly during wudu. What is a sensible improvement?

options.text: Increase the flow to prove greater devotion
Leave it running after finishing
Reduce the flow while still washing thoroughly
Save water by skipping required washing

questions.explanation: Using a smaller flow can reflect the careful use illustrated by the Prophet's modest amount of water, without compromising the washing.

questions.question: During prayer, someone who certainly had wudu has a vague worry about passing wind, with no clear evidence. What should they do?

options.text: Leave immediately because any worry breaks wudu
Repeat wudu after every rakah from now on
Ask everyone nearby to decide for them
Continue rather than act on mere doubt

questions.explanation: A vague worry alone does not overturn certainty. The hadith's sound and smell examples indicate certainty; they are not exclusive tests for every case.

questions.question: In congregation, a worshipper deliberately starts bowing before the imam. What should they correct?

options.text: Let the imam lead and follow his bowing
Move even earlier in the next rakah
Choose a faster worshipper to follow instead
Stop paying attention to the imam's movements

questions.explanation: The congregation is instructed to follow the imam, rather than deliberately precede him.

questions.question: You hear the prayer underway as you approach the mosque. Which response follows the Prophetic guidance?

options.text: Run through people to avoid missing another second
Walk calmly, join the prayer and complete what you missed
Return home because joining late is never allowed
Demand that the imam restart for you

questions.explanation: Calm arrival and joining what one catches are the actions taught in the cited report.

questions.question: A friend starts a casual chat while the imam is delivering the Friday khutbah. What is the best response?

options.text: Continue quietly for the whole sermon
Start a long discussion about the rules of silence
Stop the conversation and attend to the khutbah
Send voice messages about the conversation

questions.explanation: The hadith stresses listening and warns against speech during the sermon, even a spoken instruction to a companion to be quiet.

questions.question: Someone already observes the obligatory prayers and wants to establish more daily worship. Which habit fits the cited encouragement?

options.text: Drop an obligatory prayer to make room for extra ones
Pray additional rakahs only when an audience is present
Assume additional prayer is never encouraged
Learn and maintain the regular additional prayers

questions.explanation: The report encourages a regular practice of additional daily rakahs alongside the obligatory prayers.

questions.question: A Ramadan planner marks only the twenty-seventh night for worship and ignores the other final odd nights. What would improve it?

options.text: Include the other odd nights of the final ten as well
Move the search entirely to the first week
Assume Laylat al-Qadr occurs every Friday
Replace all night worship with a countdown

questions.explanation: The cited instruction is to seek the night across the odd nights of the last ten, rather than restrict the search to one assumed date.

questions.question: Someone plans a voluntary fast on Eid al-Fitr itself to earn extra reward. What should they do?

options.text: Fast because a voluntary intention overrides the prohibition
Choose a permissible day instead of fasting on Eid
Fast only until the Eid prayer finishes
Fast if they do not tell anyone

questions.explanation: Fasting on Eid al-Fitr itself is prohibited in the cited report, even when intended as extra worship.

questions.question: A person's extra worship is leading them to neglect their family's legitimate needs. Which advice fits the teaching approved by the Prophet?

options.text: Assume extra worship excuses every neglected responsibility
Tell the family that they no longer have any rights
Organize extra worship while giving family and self their due rights
Abandon all worship to avoid planning difficulties

questions.explanation: Salman's advice, approved by the Prophet, joins devotion to Allah with fulfilling the rights of oneself and one's family.

questions.question: A household has left arrangements for zakat al-fitr until the last moment. Which practical step best follows the reported timing?

options.text: Schedule delivery for several weeks after Eid by default
Replace delivery with a social-media announcement
Assume deciding to give is the same as delivering it
Use a reliable arrangement that delivers it before the Eid prayer

questions.explanation: The scenario applies the report's timing instruction. A reliable arrangement should account for actual delivery rather than intention alone.

questions.question: A person wonders whether zakah is due on their savings. What is a responsible next step?

options.text: Check the applicable wealth conditions and eligible recipients with reliable guidance
Pay the same amount as a friend without checking anything
Assume every purchase counts as zakah
Decide solely from the number of years they have used a bank

questions.explanation: The hadith establishes qualifying thresholds for specified wealth, while Quran 9:60 identifies recipient categories. An individual assessment requires the relevant details.

questions.question: While preparing food donations, someone sets aside spoiled items they would refuse themselves. What should change?

options.text: Hide the spoiled items under better ones
Choose wholesome food suitable for the recipients
Assume charity makes spoiled food wholesome
Give the spoiled items first to clear storage

questions.explanation: The verse warns against deliberately giving inferior things one would be reluctant to accept. Donations should be fit for their intended use.

questions.question: A donor can quietly help a poor household without publishing their names. Which choice reflects the verse's praise of private giving?

options.text: Insist that the household advertise the donor
Refuse to help unless the gift is filmed
Give discreetly without seeking public credit
Publish private details to make the gift count

questions.explanation: Quran 2:271 praises giving privately to the poor. The scenario applies that encouragement to a discreet donation.

questions.question: After making dua for some time, someone wants to stop because the request has not been granted yet. What reminder fits the hadith?

options.text: An unanswered request proves dua is useless
Allah must grant the exact request by a human deadline
Only the first attempt at dua has any value
Keep turning to Allah and avoid impatiently giving up

questions.explanation: The report warns against impatience expressed as having asked without receiving an answer.

questions.question: Someone remembers Allah while walking to work and wonders if remembrance is restricted to sitting after prayer. Which answer fits the verse?

options.text: Remembrance can accompany daily life, not just one posture or setting
Only remembrance after prayer can ever count
Walking prevents a person from remembering Allah
A mosque seat is required for all remembrance

questions.explanation: The verse describes remembrance while standing, sitting and lying down. This supports remembrance beyond one setting.

questions.question: You want to respond to the Quran's instruction concerning the Prophet. Which action fits?

options.text: Ask him to share Allah's divinity
Ask Allah to bless him and send greetings of peace
Treat his guidance as irrelevant
Replace prayer to Allah with praise of a person

questions.explanation: The verse directs believers to send blessings and greetings of peace upon the Prophet.

questions.question: Someone prays Fajr's two Sunnah rakahs and assumes the obligatory prayer is now covered. What should they understand?

options.text: Any two morning rakahs automatically fulfil both
The obligatory prayer applies only if the Sunnah is missed
The Sunnah prayer and the obligatory prayer are distinct
The Sunnah prayer removes all prayer duties until midday

questions.explanation: The two Sunnah rakahs have great merit, while the obligatory daily prayers remain a separate duty.

questions.question: A person notices they rush through prayer while thinking about their phone. Which improvement best reflects humble attentiveness?

options.text: Make the movements faster to finish sooner
Keep checking messages between movements
Focus on whether others admire the prayer
Put distractions aside and give the prayer calm attention

questions.explanation: The Quran praises humble attentiveness in prayer, and the cited hadith teaches completing prayer movements calmly.
